issue.title: A usage window with no `used` reads as 0% — which also puts a spent account first in the routing order
issue.body:
## What happens

A provider plugin that leaves out `used` on its usage windows makes a **spent account read as full**, and — because `used` is what the routing order sorts by — it puts that account at the **front** of the route. On my machine a Loomy account with `0` credits was picked 255 out of 256 times over three days, and 11 of those requests failed with the vendor's "insufficient credits".

Two separate things combine here. Both are in the plugin contract today; the second one is the one I'd like to see changed.

## 1. `used` is missing ⇒ silently treated as `0`

`usageOf()` normalises with:

```js
used: Math.max(0, num(w?.used)),   // past 100 when overspent
```

Nothing distinguishes "the plugin says 0% used" from "the plugin didn't say". So a plugin that only sends `display`/`amount` (which is what the two Loomy plugins on npm do — one of them literally cannot get the ceiling, see below) gets `used: 0` on every window.

The Settings meter has a "how much is left" toggle, and it reads:

```js
function quotaFill(w){ const used = Math.round(to100(w.used)); return quotaLeft ? 100 - used : used }
```

⇒ the card shows **"0 积分 · 剩余 100%"** — the number from `display`, the percentage from a field that was never sent.

**Suggestion:** treat an absent `used` as *unknown* rather than `0` — e.g. carry `used: null` through, and have the meter show an indeterminate bar / the `display` text only. At minimum, don't let an absent `used` mean "full".

## 2. `used` (so an absent one) is a routing input

```js
const group = (w) => w.used >= 98 ? "spent" : w.used >= 90 ? "low" : "fine"
```

and the smart-routing explanation for `spent` is *"all but used up, it answers only when nothing else can"*.

So an absent `used` doesn't merely misdraw a bar — it **reorders the route**. That's a costly failure mode for exactly the accounts people care about (a plan that ran out).

**Suggestion:** a window that didn't state `used` should not participate in the `spent`/`low` ranking (like `aside` windows already don't), instead of ranking as `fine`.

## 3. (minor) check-in `outcome` outside the enum is rewritten to `failed`, and its message is kept

```js
const checkinOutcomes = ["claimed", "done", "ineligible", "inactive", "captcha", "failed"]
if (!checkinOutcomes.includes(r.outcome)) {
  return { outcome: "failed", credit: 0, streak: 0,
           message: message || `the plugin answered no outcome (${JSON.stringify(r.outcome ?? null)})` }
}
```

One of the Loomy plugins on npm returns `{ outcome: "success", message: "每日赠送积分已刷新" }`. Not in the enum ⇒ rewritten to `failed`, **with its message kept**, so the UI reads *"签到失败 · 每日赠送积分已刷新"* — "check-in failed · credits refreshed". The check-in actually succeeds every day.

**Suggestion:** when the outcome is unrecognised, keep the plugin's message but prefix it, so the two halves can't be read as a contradiction (or surface the raw value in the message when one is present, not only when it isn't).

## Reproduction (no plugin needed)

`usage()` returning `{ windows: [{ name: "x", display: "0 / 5000" }] }` is enough to see (1) and (2): the card shows "100% left" and the account sorts before accounts reporting real percentages.

## Context

I wrote a Loomy plugin that reports the two pools properly (the daily pool counted, the permanent pool `aside`) and the measured result here was: the spent account moved from **3/13 → 13/13** in the routing order, was **rested by window** until the next Beijing day (`rest: {by: "window", until: "2026-10-27T00:05:00+08:00"}`), and the never-picked-again count went from 255 to 0. So the mechanism works exactly as designed **once `used` is actually sent** — the request here is only about the case where a plugin doesn't send it.

Happy to send a PR for any of these if you tell me which shape you prefer (for (1): `used: null` vs. dropping the window vs. an explicit `unknown: true`).

Verified against magpie `0.1.1254` (Windows amd64 build, 2026-10-25).

comments.body:
Both halves come from the same coercion: `host.js`'s `usageOf` did `used: Math.max(0, num(w?.used))`, so absent became 0; Go's `UsageWindow.Used float64` could not carry absence either; that 0 became a `QuotaWindow` with a used of 0, which the meter read as "100% left" (and as `NaN%` where the page had no used at all) and which `allowanceOf` put at the front of the smart-routing order - an account that is spent ranking as the one with the most left.

Fixed on [fix/usage-absent-used](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/usage-absent-used) (`6791aa99`, on `01468003`):
- `host.js` passes an absent `used` through as `null`; `plugin.UsageWindow.Used` is a `*float64`, so absent and 0 are different values end to end.
- `quotaOfPlugin` marks such a window `Text` (its `display` only) and `Aside` (no share in the allowance), and `allowanceOf` skips both - a window that said nothing no longer ranks as "fine". An account whose windows all say nothing has no `Allowance`, so routing leaves it unknown instead of preferring it.
- `app.js` gained `quotaNoShare`: no `used` (or a text-only window) draws its display text or "No allowance reported", never a meter, never `NaN`, and takes no part in the pace.
- the check-in's unrecognised outcome keeps the plugin's message but names the plugin's own word first: `the plugin answered "yes": 每日赠送积分已刷新`, instead of "check-in failed · credits refreshed".

RED -> GREEN, re-run independently here:
- clean base with only the tests: the browser test fails on Chromium and WebKit with `0 / 5000 · NaN% used` and a meter drawn; the Go regression `TestAWindowWithoutUsedIsNoAllowance` fails with both windows in the allowance, `Credits` (never said `used`) beside `Daily` (said 0).
- at the head: the browser test passes 2/2, the Go tests pass, and a window that said `used: 0` is still an allowance while one that said nothing is not.
- `go test ./internal/provider` and `./internal/plugin` pass with two known failures skipped: `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` (fatal `close of synctest channel from outside bubble`) and `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, both red on the clean base too. `go vet` and `go build` for linux, windows and `-tags nogui` pass; `gofmt -l` is empty.

Why two commits on the branch: the first test builds `Used: fptr(0)`, which the base's `float64` field cannot express, so the second commit adds a regression whose own code avoids `fptr` - a plugin reply decoded as the host sends it. That is the one shown failing above, and it reproduces the failure when added to the clean base on its own; the branch's test file as a whole does not compile there, since it shares a file with the `fptr` test.

Limits: the routing outcome is asserted at `quotaOfPlugin`/`allowanceOf`, not through a live request to a real vendor; no real plugin on this machine reports a window without `used`; the check-in prefix is tested through the host's fake provider. Playwright is not vendored in this checkout - the browser test ran on this machine's 1.64.1 (Chromium and WebKit) via `NODE_PATH`. Nothing in `internal/gui`'s Go package tests was run.

Fixed in v0.1.1608 (9733ed1b4). Thanks to skygunner for the fix: it was ported from the `fix/usage-absent-used` branch, with credit in the commit.

A plugin usage window that leaves out `used` is no longer read as 0:
- The card shows the plugin's own text, or "No allowance reported", with no percentage and no meter. It no longer says "100% left" or NaN%.
- Smart routing treats such an account as not known yet, so it no longer puts spent accounts first. This holds for a fresh reading and for the one magpie kept on disk.
- A window that does say `used: 0` still reads as 0%.

The branch's check-in wording change went in its own commit (51202cd43).

I'm keeping this open until you confirm it works for your accounts.

Confirming late. You asked for a confirmation on my accounts and I closed this on 2026-10-27 without writing one — that was my mistake, so here is the sentence.

**Version.** magpie `0.1.1756`, Windows amd64. That is past `9733ed1b` / v0.1.1608, and I checked the commit's diff against the tree I run, so what I am running is the code you shipped: `plugin.UsageWindow.Used` is a `*float64`, `quotaOfPlugin` marks a window with no `used` as Text + Aside, and `routedAllowance` keeps such an account out of the ranking rather than ranking it as "all left".

**What I cannot give you.** The account-side red→green. My reproducer was a Loomy account whose plugin sent only `display`/`amount`; in the install that runs today that plugin reports `used` on both pools, so the "no `used`" state does not occur here any more and I have no card reading to show you. At close time I had also not recorded the before/after reading.

So the close rests on the fix being in the build I run, not on a fresh measurement of my own. If the shape turns up again in one of my plugins I will reopen with the log rather than another silent close.

issue.title: gui test: key-balance-card's 5s first-paint wait times out in WebKit under a full run

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Seen in a 56-file GUI run (concurrency 6) at 51202cd43 (v0.1.1608, #3650 work). The test passes 20 of 20 alone, both at that head and at 9298d2a7c, so it is a timing assumption, not that change.

```
  ...
# Subtest: webkit zh-TW: a key's balance is on its plan's card, two keys, a failed and a stale balance
ok 186 - webkit zh-TW: a key's balance is on its plan's card, two keys, a failed and a stale balance
  ---
  duration_ms: 9002.928375
  type: 'test'
  ...
# Subtest: webkit ja: a key's balance is on its plan's card, the reporter's key
not ok 187 - webkit ja: a key's balance is on its plan's card, the reporter's key
  ---
  duration_ms: 15318.515208
  type: 'test'
  location: 'internal/gui/tests/key-balance-card.test.cjs:103:7'
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: 'page.waitForFunction: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.'
  code: 'ERR_TEST_FAILURE'
  name: 'TimeoutError'
  stack: |-
    TestContext.<anonymous> (internal/gui/tests/key-balance-card.test.cjs:117:22)
  ...
# Subtest: webkit ja: a key's balance is on its plan's card, two keys, a failed and a stale balance
```

Cause to look at: `page.setDefaultTimeout(5000)` covers the first paint of the panel (`waitForFunction` for `#panelQuota .pq-card[data-card]`, line 117). A cold WebKit page under load takes longer than 5s to get there (this case ran 15.3s). Code standards: a timing test leaves room on both sides; the wait should be on state with a ceiling that fits a loaded machine, as other GUI tests use.

issue.title: WorkBuddy 积分的失效时间到不了卡片：QuotaSpan 把 runsOutAt 丢了

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
Confirmed on my setup — it reads right. Closed.

Built `origin/main` at 8f023b51 (v0.1.1623, which carries b9ab1723) and ran it against a copy of my config with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` pointed at the copy, so the instance I use daily was untouched. Then sent one real request through that gateway to a group that routes `free first`, which is what makes the gateway fill `.free` at all (routing.go:1597, only under `st.ByFree`), and opened the Routing page in a browser.

What the page does now, in zh:

- the four seats the trace carries as `free: true` show 「免费 · 不花额度」 and their row is `class="nobar"` — no bar, no percentage.
- a paid seat beside them still shows its share (「已用 75%」 and its bar), and the one that is resting still says its rest first (「额度用尽 · 58 分钟后恢复」).

Both points in your message are right, and they were the ones I had wrong: `.free` does arrive only with a routing that weighs by it, so my fixture described a shape the gateway never sends, and my German string did fail `/verbraucht/`. Building the case on the real shape was the fix.

One thing worth knowing for whoever reads this next, not a defect: `FreeModel` (models.go:1697) also answers free when a model's four prices are all 0, not only when the plugin lists it free. So a seat serving a model whose plugin declares `input: 0, output: 0` reads 「不花额度」 even under a paid subscription tier — that's two of my four free seats here (`qoder/dfmodel`, under a `personal_standard` account). The word is accurate for what the vendor charges; the account's own windows are what the other models on it draw from, which is exactly the confusion this issue was about.

Thanks for taking it, and for the co-author credit.

issue.title: usage: a prepaid wallet has no way to say "how much is left" — a window forces a fake share, no window makes the account unknown

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## TL;DR

A provider that sells **prepaid credit** — a wallet — cannot be described by the current usage contract:

- **With windows**, `used` must be a share of a periodic allowance. A wallet has no such denominator, so any `used` we send is fabricated.
- **Without windows**, `routedAllowance` returns not-ok, `weighed()` leaves `Known` unset, and the Routing page says 「剩余额度未知」 — the account ranks after every known one (#3650).
- **`aside: true` does not help**: `allowanceOf()` skips those windows whole, with the same result.

What is missing is a **balance-shaped reading**: "this much is left", in a unit, with no percentage. Two fields would carry it — `QuotaWindow.Balance` and `routes.Seat.Left`.

## The provider (real numbers, 2026-10-28)

SuperMagic (超级麦吉 / MagiCrew), community plugin `magpie-magicrew-auth`.

`GET /api/v1/quota/points/total` answers:

```json
{"total_points": 6291,
 "expiring_quota_details": [
   {"remaining_points": 185, "expires_at": "2026-10-28 23:59:59"},
   {"remaining_points": 100, "expires_at": "2026-11-26 16:45:13"},
   {"remaining_points": 956, "expires_at": "2027-11-03 19:11:01"}],
 "organization_limit_points": null,
 "user_limit_points": null,
 "next_cycle_grant": null}
```

- No total, no consumed: `*_limit_points` are `null` on personal accounts.
- The ledger endpoint `POST /api/v1/quota/points/records/queries` answers **HTTP 500** on both sites (five body shapes tried), so "how much was spent" is not readable either.
- The only fixed number is the daily login gift — **200 points/day (CN), 50 (intl)** — which expires at 23:59:59 the same day.

## What the plugin tried, and what magpie did

| plugin sends | magpie | result |
|---|---|---|
| `aside: true, used: 0, display: "6,291 积分"` | `allowanceOf()` skips Aside/Text whole; none left → `routedAllowance` not ok → `weighed()` leaves `Known` unset | Routing page 「剩余额度未知」; the account ranks after every known one |
| `used: 0, display: "6,291 积分"` (no `limit`) | known, but routing's `quota()` shows the count only when `limit > 0` | row reads `0% used`, no figure |
| `used: 0, amount: 0, limit: 6291` | known, figure shown | percentage is `0 / 6291` — a tautology (denominator = remainder); the "fake share" of #3353 |

## What it costs the router

`routes.Seat` carries `Used float64` (a 0–100 share), `Soon []time.Time`, `Lapse`, `Pace`, … — **nothing that says how much is left**.

- **`pace`**: `(100 - used) / hours until resetsAt`. A wallet has no `resetsAt` and its `used` is always 0, so every account of this provider gets **the same pace**. 6,291 points and 750 points are indistinguishable.
- **`smart`**: the fine tier is ordered by `Soon` (`Allowance.Renewal`, which does fold `runsOutAt` in), then `Lapse` — it can say *whose points expire first*, never *who has more left*.

Measured on 4 accounts: 1,363 / 1,693 / 6,291 / 750 points; earliest expiries 178 / 29 / 29 / 372 days out. Under `smart` all four tie on `Soon` whenever the expiry days match; under `pace` they are **exactly** identical.

## Suggested shape

**`QuotaWindow`**

```go
// Balance is how much of this allowance is left, in Unit — a reading of a
// prepaid balance, with no share to tell (Used stays nil for it).
Balance *float64 `json:"balance,omitempty"`
```

`allowanceOf` keeps such a window (`l.Balance = *w.Balance`), so `Known` is true, without inventing a `Used`.

**`routes.Seat`**

```go
// Left is the absolute remainder in the provider's own unit: comparable
// within one provider, 0 when the vendor doesn't say.
Left float64
```

Filled from the windows' `Balance` (or the fullest window's `Amount`/`Of` when the vendor does count).

**Ordering**: `smart` / `pace` fall back to `Left` (most first) when shares are unknown or equal. A prepaid provider then becomes rankable by both dimensions that matter: *who runs out first* (`runsOutAt`) and *who has the most left* (`balance`).

## Today's plugin-side workaround (for reference)

Three windows, so the account is at least known and carries `runsOutAt`:

1. **今日积分** — today's batch, **real percentage** (denominator = the 200/50 daily gift), `resetsAt` = next midnight.
2. **限时积分** — the rest of the expiring batches, `used: 0`, `limit` = current remainder, `runsOutAt` = earliest.
3. **永久积分** — `total − Σexpiring`, `aside`, display only.

That is the best the current contract allows — and it still cannot express "how much".

## Related

- #3428 — the seat knows *when* but not *how much* is lost (`w.RunsOut` dropped in `allowanceOf`). This issue is the same gap one layer up: the seat also cannot see *how much is left at all*.
- #3352 — a `Windows: []` reading with a balance is dropped entirely, so the account is unknown.
- #3353 — a window that never moves reads as `used: 0` and distorts smart ordering.
- #3650 — a window without `used` becomes text + aside, no share.

Happy to send a PR for the two fields if the shape looks right — I can test it against this provider directly.

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
49c99e18d (#4612, ggbdpq) makes quota history draw a window set aside for routing, and marks Factory's "Extra usage" `Text` so it isn't drawn as a line.

`pointOf` (internal/provider/quota_history.go) still draws any window that isn't Text, Unlimited or a Family, has a name, and has a Used that isn't NaN. A plugin's aside row that has only a display or an amount, and no used share, comes in with Used 0, so it is drawn as a flat 100% left line. Factory was fixed at its source. Every other plugin that reports such a row has the same problem.

Possible fixes: skip a window with no Used reading (that needs a way to tell "0 used" from "not said"), or have the plugin usage reader mark such rows Text. Found in the review of #4612. Not reproduced with a real plugin.

issue.title: Pace routing can start a long tool turn on a stale allowance after idle; default turn affinity preserves that choice after refresh

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### Summary

On a remote Magpie installation with two Grok subscription accounts and `routing: "pace"`, the first request after an idle period used an older routing allowance even though quota history already contained a newer reading. The old value put the accounts in the same 10% pace band, so the recent-token tie-break selected Account B. The next request had the fresh allowance, but default within-turn affinity kept B first for the rest of a 104-request tool turn.

I understand that pace does not promise equal percentages or equal request counts, and that within-turn affinity protects continuity. The issue is the amplification of a stale initial routing decision, rather than an arithmetic error in the pace formula.

### Environment and scope

- Version at inspection: Magpie v0.1.2737, Docker, Linux.
- Source inspected: `17c465375da7211ad3e4fab268370ade353b6675`.
- Grok plugin: `@magpie-community/opencode-grok-auth` 0.2.3.
- Two enabled accounts, provider `routing: "pace"`, affinity omitted/default.
- Rotation/routing plugins enabled; account cap stop/careful disabled.
- `quotaReads` is not set to `asked`.
- The evidence is from retained production traces on November 2, inspected on November 3. The exact binary version that wrote every earlier trace was not independently established.
- This was a read-only investigation; no synthetic model calls or live reproduction were performed.

### Observed sequence

All times are UTC on 2026-11-02. Account A resets on November 4 at 08:56:31; B resets at 03:31:46.

1. At **13:47:39**, quota history already records B as **45% used** (`left: 55`).
2. At **14:14:15.486**, the first request of a new conversation has:

```json
{
  "affinity": {"mode": "", "turn": 1, "why": "first"},
  "order": [
    {"account": "B", "used": 29, "pace": 1.9038964947, "recentTokens": 3.699833445e-19},
    {"account": "A", "used": 11, "pace": 2.0840862367, "recentTokens": 2.642310263}
  ],
  "servedBy": "B"
}
```

These snippets are field-selected and anonymized from the trace; `account`, `recentTokens`, and `servedBy` are explanatory names. B/A pace is about 0.9135, so selecting B by the recent-token tie-break is consistent with the 10% band rule **given the stale 29% input**.

3. At **14:14:19.016**, the next request now knows B is **45% used**:

```json
{
  "affinity": {"mode": "", "turn": 1, "within": true, "kept": true, "why": "turn"},
  "order": [
    {"account": "B", "used": 45, "pace": 1.4748882005},
    {"account": "A", "used": 11, "pace": 2.0841341190}
  ],
  "servedBy": "B"
}
```

B is now well below the 90% band threshold relative to A, but affinity keeps B first. This conversation contains **104 requests**, one `first` and 103 `turn`, all served by B.

The source traces are lines 4822–4823 of the decompressed `routing/2026-11-02.jsonl.gz`.

A separate conversation at 14:48 initially selected A correctly, then failed over to B after one A-side 502. It stayed on B even after A's recorded backoff expired. Later independent conversations selected A successfully. Thus this is not a permanently unavailable A or a permanently fixed B-first order.

### Relevant implementation

- `internal/provider/routing.go:651–755`: `Allowances` refreshes asynchronously after a minute. An already-known agent does not wait for that refresh, so its current request can use the old `usedCache` map.
- `internal/provider/login_usage.go:235–306`: the per-login reading has a separate one-minute cache.
- `internal/routes/strategies.go:340–411`: pace bands within 10%, then recent usage.
- `internal/gateway/affinity.go:644–674`: default within-turn affinity can move the previous account ahead of a better pace candidate.
- Codex has an additional live update path in `internal/provider/codex_limits.go`, updating both usage and routing caches from response observations. I did not find an equivalent Grok weekly-billing observation path.

### Expected behavior / possible improvement

A new conversation after idle should avoid establishing affinity from a substantially older allowance when a newer successful reading is available. Possible approaches include consuming newer cached readings before returning the routing snapshot, or a bounded freshness wait for a new conversation/turn. A trace field showing allowance age and the pre-affinity candidate would also make this easier to diagnose.

I am not proposing that every request block on billing, or that default within-turn affinity be removed globally. An explicit policy for very large allowance differences could be considered separately.

For a regression test, a fixture could seed an older routing allowance of B=29% and a newer login reading of B=45%, while A=11%, then exercise the first request and subsequent tool continuation. The timestamps and pace values above come from retained traces; the proposed fixture has not been implemented or run.

### Limits of the conclusion

The account's billing percentage also increased during periods with no corresponding requests in this gateway's retained ledger. Therefore this report does **not** attribute the entire account percentage gap to Magpie. There were also intermittent 0% usage observations; the raw billing responses were not captured, so their origin remains unconfirmed and is separate from the stale-29% sequence above.

### Related reports checked

- #1295: Codex quota freshness/cap behavior.
- #1313: background usage observations reaching history.
- #2230: implicit-cache affinity.
- #3938: conversation identity collisions; not established in this case.
- #3650: absent plugin `used` values interpreted as zero.

I did not find a direct duplicate of the idle stale allowance plus long-turn amplification case in the searches performed.
